title: The Fake Signal
briefing_md:
Campus Nexus is the smart-building system of a fictional university. It watches 2,400 sensors across the hostels.

At 3:12 AM on Thursday 16 October, it raised a FIRE alarm for Hostel Block C, third floor. The automatic sirens woke 600 students, who stood outside in the cold for 40 minutes. The fire team found no smoke, no heat and no fire.

The wardens say sensor C3-SMK-114 has been faulty for weeks and want it replaced. The dean wants to know if that is really what happened, and whether it could happen again tomorrow night.
root_cause_options: Human error during an approved change
Bad or wrongly formatted input data
Test or staging activity hitting production
twist_md: The QA team has shared the log of their overnight CI pipeline and a message from their channel the next morning.

content.prompt: Why did the fire alarm trigger in Hostel C at 03:12?
content.output:
Most probable cause: hardware malfunction of smoke sensor C3-SMK-114.
Supporting signals: open maintenance ticket MT-2290 (chirping), battery replaced 13 days ago, reading of 812 ppm without any neighbouring sensor rising.
Recommended action: replace C3-SMK-114 and close the incident.

lines: 03:12:06 INFO  siren  EVACUATE zone=C floors=ALL (source: bms rule fire-single)
03:52:40 INFO  siren  reset by fire-team (manual key)

content.body_md: Arrived 03:19. Block C floors 1–4 inspected with thermal camera. No smoke, no heat source, no burning smell. Sensor C3-SMK-114 tested on site with test spray: responds normally, reading 4 ppm in clean air. All clear at 03:48.

content.subject: Night fire drill, Block C — report and recording
content.body_md: The night drill in Block C started at 03:12 using a smoke generator near C3-SMK-114. All sensor traffic from 03:00–03:30 was recorded (drill-2026-08-14.jsonl) and shared with QA for future load testing.

messages.text: We moved the nightly load test to the new CI yesterday evening. Did anyone copy over the BROKER_URL secret? On the old CI it pointed to bms-staging.
…no. And the tool falls back to prod when it's empty. Oh no.

answer.root_cause_md: Before the twist, the maintenance tickets, wardens' chat and the AI diagnosis all blame sensor C3-SMK-114. Careful teams notice the alarm message carries a 14 August timestamp and an out-of-order sequence number (E03, E04), was published by nx-sim-02 from a CI runner (E05, E12), matches the recorded fire drill (E10), and that the replay tool defaults to the production broker (E11). The fire team found the sensor working (E09).
answer.post_twist_category: Test or staging activity hitting production
answer.post_twist_responsible: The QA nightly load test, moved to a new CI platform, ran without its BROKER_URL secret, so the replay tool fell back to the production MQTT broker and replayed the 14 August fire-drill recording; the production broker accepted anonymous publishes and the fire rule needed only one sensor.
